Samir Patel: Hey team, opening my very first PR — tiny docs tweak + a logging config change. Quick onboarding questions: 1) Which branch should I target for non-urgent docs/config changes (main vs release/*)? 2) Do we prefer squashed commits for small edits? 3) Any specific commit message template to follow?

Tasha Nguyen: Welcome! For non-urgent stuff like that, target main. release/* branches are reserved for hotfixes that need to land in the next patch.

Tasha Nguyen: We usually squash small PRs to keep history tidy. If the PR contains clear separate steps that are helpful to preserve, keep them. Rule of thumb: if < ~5 tiny commits and all related, squash. :slightly_smiling_face:

Tasha Nguyen: Commit message format we like: <area>(<scope>): <short summary>

Example:
```
docs(readme): clarify auth setup for local dev

Also adjust logging default to info to reduce noise.
```

Mike Chen: Don't forget pre-commit hooks and CI expectations. Before pushing/opening run:
```
pre-commit run --all-files
make test-local  # lint + fast unit subset
```
If CI shows failures, fix locally first — saves a bunch of CI churn.

Olivia Rivera: Check CODEOWNERS to see auto-assigned reviewers. For runtime changes ping @eng-runtime, for docs ping @devex. Add labels like `type/docs` and `size/XS` (or `size/S` if it grows).

Olivia Rivera: Also complete the PR template: short description, why, and one QA step (e.g., "ran make test-local, no new failures"). That speeds reviews.

ci-bot: CI status: queued -> running (build/ci: unit-tests)

Samir Patel: Thanks! One more: branch naming convention?

Mike Chen: We prefer `<yourname>/pr/<short-summary>` or `<yourname>/fix/<short-summary>` for small changes. Example: `samir/pr/kv-log-level`.

Mike Chen: If you need to squash locally: 
```
git rebase -i HEAD~N  # squash as needed
git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>
```

Tasha Nguyen: Review SLA: aim for 24-48h turnaround. If you need faster, add `review/fast` label and ping reviewers in the PR comment.

Samir Patel: Great, I'll target main, squash, follow the commit format, run pre-commit and tests, and request reviewers via CODEOWNERS. Thanks for the warm welcome! :wave:
